about: Living Roots Wine & Co. was founded in 2016 by Sebastian and Colleen Hardy, and makes wine in two hemispheres. Seb comes from six generations of Australian winemakers; Colleen, from just outside Rochester, left marketing for the cellar and met him while working a vintage in South Australia. The couple opened Rochester’s only urban winery on University Avenue in late 2017, making Finger Lakes whites and sparkling wines from local growers and reds in the Adelaide Hills, and in 2023 Halliday’s Wine Companion named Living Roots Australia’s Best New Winery.

Pinot Gris, the same grape Italians call Pinot Grigio, has grey-pink skins and, in a cool climate like the Finger Lakes, gives whites with real aromatic lift and texture. For this wine the Hardys let the juice ferment naturally, on its own wild yeasts, in stainless steel, then left it resting on its lees, the spent yeast, for ten months to build a fuller, rounder palate. It was finished completely dry.

2021 was a cooler Finger Lakes vintage, and the winemakers describe a style that is rich but fresh: high-toned aromatics and the varietal’s classic ripe-pear character, a gingery spice, and bright acidity holding the richness in balance. Living Roots has made Pinot Gris in most vintages since; reviewing the 2020, VinePair’s Keith Beavers noted a full, fruit-forward nose and a rich, structured palate.
